walkthroughs.body_html:
Programming Paradigms — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Programming Paradigms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Programming Paradigms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the scope of a local variable?
options: Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
Accessible only within the function/block where it is declared.
It is impossible to break.
Accessible everywhere in the program.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
It is impossible to break.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Optimal substructure”?
options: Solves problems by storing solutions to overlapping subproblems to avoid recomputation.
Property that optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions to subproblems.
Same subproblem appears multiple times - the trait that makes DP worthwhile.
Classic DP example; naive recursion is O(2^n) but DP gives O(n).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Overlapping subproblems”?
options: Solves problems by storing solutions to overlapping subproblems to avoid recomputation.
Same subproblem appears multiple times - the trait that makes DP worthwhile.
Bottom-up DP filling a table iteratively from base cases to the target.
Top-down DP: cache results of recursive calls so each subproblem is solved once.
